newsitem.title: HAITI: U.S. Support Group extends mission in Haiti.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Support Group extends mission in Haiti.

text.p: U.S. officials have decided to keep a 450-member military support mission in Haiti for the time being, a military spokesman said Tuesday, two days after a June 1 deadline for their departure passed.
"We have been told by higher headquarters that we are to continue with our mission until further directive," said Lt. Stewart Upton, public relations officer for the U.S. Support Group-Haiti.
"The appropriate requests for funding have been submitted and we are confident that funding will be provided to continue the U.S. Support Group-Haiti work," he said.

The support group, which includes soldiers from the U.S. Army's Fort Bragg, U.S. Coast Guard crew members and U.S. Navy medics and engineers, trains military units in Haiti and provides medical care to U.N. personnel.
It has also built roads and renovated schools, provided training to the Haitian Coast Guard and assisted in drug interdiction efforts, U.S. officials said.
Members of the mission are expected to remain at least until the end of the U.N. mission in Haiti on July 31.

Haiti's streets are being patrolled by 700 Canadian soldiers and 500 Pakistani troops funded by the United States. An estimated 300 U.S., French, Canadian and Algerian police officers are training the Haitian National Police.
Haitian popular organisations have demonstrated in recent months against the foreign military presence, which they view as an occupation of their country.

Foreign troops have been patrolling Haiti since September 1994, when a force of 20,000 U.S. troops led an occupation that ended a military dictatorship and restored the Caribbean nation's elected government.
